description: We are a team composed by an experienced geologist Miriela Ulloa, two software developers Juan Labrada and Railson De Oliveira Silva and a student in computer sciences Luis Labrada. We are interested in the development of Applications that help NASA solve difficult problems.
summary:
Our project, Find training places, aims to identify terrestrial environments that can provide useful analogues for studying future human settlements on the Moon and technologies for subsurface water exploration.

We developed a first version of a geospatial application with the assistance of Claude, integrating publicly available scientific datasets, including basaltic rock distributions, air temperature, precipitation, permafrost, ground ice content, cave entrances, lava tubes, and volcanic craters.

The application explores two complementary objectives:

- *Water exploration:* identifying terrestrial environments with frozen ground, subsurface ice, and geological conditions that can help study and test drilling and water-prospecting technologies relevant to lunar exploration.
- *Future lunar settlements.....:* identifying geological structures such as caves and lava tubes that could provide natural protection against radiation and meteorite impacts, as well as other environmental characteristics relevant to settlement planning.

This preliminary version demonstrates how open scientific datasets and artificial intelligence can be combined in a geospatial tool to identify, compare, and evaluate potential terrestrial analogues, supporting research and preparation for future lunar missions.

Detailed Project Description:

We developed a first version of a geospatial application that identifies and compares terrestrial environments that could serve as analogs for future lunar settlements and the exploration of subsurface water. The application works by integrating and visualizing publicly available scientific data, such as temperature, precipitation, basaltic rocks, permafrost, ground ice content, cave entrances, lava tubes, and volcanic craters. This data makes it possible to explore regions with conditions of interest for studying drilling and the search for water, as well as natural structures that could offer protection against radiation and meteorite impacts. Its main benefit is bringing together information from different sources in a single tool, making it easier to identify potential analog sites. We hope to expand its features and refine the selection criteria to support future research and lunar missions. To develop the application, we used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI assistant to generate and organize the code and build the first version of the tool.
